cards.front: Recall a key point about Papers and Boards
cards.back: Cartridge paper: 120-300 gsm, textured surface, good for sketching and marker work.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Papers and Boards
cards.back: Corrugated board: two liner layers with fluted medium - excellent crush resistance, lightweight, used for packaging.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Papers and Boards
cards.back: Foam-core board: polystyrene foam sandwiched between card layers - very lightweight, rigid, easy to cut; used for architectural models.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Papers and Boards
cards.back: Solid white board: high-quality bleached board, 200+ gsm - smooth surface for printing and packaging.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Papers and Boards
cards.back: Tracing paper: translucent, 40-90 gsm - used for overlay work, developing ideas, transferring designs.

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: When justifying paper/board choices, use SFP: Surface (smooth/textured), Function (rigidity, foldability, protection), Process (printing method, die-cutting compatibility). Always match the material to the specific product requirements.

cards.back: Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Thicker paper is always better because it is stronger and more professional. Correct: Thickness must suit the function: tissue paper is perfect for delicate gift wrap; tracing paper needs translucency; cartridge paper needs weight and texture. Over-specifying GSM wastes material and increases cost.
A company is designing packaging for a luxury perfume bottle. Justify the choice of board materials for both the inner protective insert and the outer presentation box.

AQA D&T 8552: Written exam 50% + NEA 50%. AOs: AO1 Recall (20%), AO2 Apply (30%), AO3 Analyse & evaluate (50%). For grade 9, show perceptive understanding of how paper/board properties serve specific packaging functions.
